subtopics.title: From Growth to Decay — the Two Depreciation Formulae

questions.question: The reducing-balance depreciation formula is:
A bakkie of R240 000 depreciates straight-line at 15% p.a. After 4 years it is worth:
The same bakkie on reducing balance at 15% p.a. for 4 years is worth:
Reducing-balance value can never reach zero because:
options: Each year multiplies the current value by 0,85, which shrinks it but cannot kill it
Depreciation stops after five years by law
The formula only works for whole years

questions.question: For 9% p.a. compounded monthly over 2 years, the correct i and n are:
R10 000 at 9% p.a. compounded monthly grows in 2 years to:
At the same quoted rate, monthly compounding beats annual because:
options: Each month's interest joins the principal immediately and starts earning interest itself
The monthly rate is higher than the annual rate
Banks add a bonus for monthly accounts
The formula uses a bigger P

questions.question: The most common finance error in the paper is:
options: Forgetting to convert rand to cents
Rounding the final answer to two decimals
Mixing periods — a monthly rate with n in years, or an annual rate with n in months

questions.question: The effective annual rate of 9% p.a. compounded monthly is about:
The relationship between effective and nominal rates is:
Bank A offers 9,4% compounded annually; Bank B offers 9,3% compounded quarterly. The better offer is:
options: Bank A, because 9,4 is bigger than 9,3
Impossible to compare without knowing the deposit
Bank B, whose effective rate of about 9,63% beats 9,4%

questions.question: If a computed effective rate comes out SMALLER than the nominal rate, it means:
options: The calculation inverted somewhere — effective exceeds nominal whenever compounding is more than annual
The bank is running a special

subtopics.title: Exchange Rates and Mixed Timeline Problems

questions.question: At R18,50 per dollar, a laptop priced at $800 costs:
When the rand weakens from R18,50 to R19,75 per dollar, imported goods:
options: Cost more in rand — feeding inflation across the economy

questions.question: A benefit of a WEAKER rand is that:
options: Overseas holidays become cheaper for South Africans
South African exports and tourism become cheaper for foreigners

questions.question: R8 000 at 10% p.a. compounded half-yearly for 3 years grows to:
In the ruler picture, straight-line depreciation removes:
options: 15% of the current value each year
The same fixed slice of the ORIGINAL value every year

questions.question: The photocopy-of-a-photocopy picture captures reducing balance because:
options: Photocopies get bigger with each copy
Each generation keeps 85% of the ONE BEFORE, not of the original
Copies are made once a month

questions.question: On reducing balance, the bakkie's fourth year loses about R22 000 while the first lost R36 000 because:
options: The owner drives less each year
Straight-line took over in year four
15% of a smaller current value is a smaller bite

questions.question: The keywords that signal the ruler model in an exam question are:
In the paydays picture, monthly compounding wins because:
options: The monthly account has a higher advertised rate
January's interest is working and earning by February instead of waiting for December
December interest is taxed more heavily

questions.question: Over 2 years on R10 000 at 9%, payday timing alone is worth about:
The clock-conversion rule for quarterly compounding is:
options: Divide the rate by 12 and count months
Keep the annual rate and count quarters
Multiply the rate by 4 and count years
Divide the rate by 4 and count quarters

questions.question: The honest caution about compounding frequency is that:
options: Each extra step of frequency helps a little less — daily barely beats monthly
Beyond monthly, extra frequency reduces the return
Frequency only matters for deposits above R100 000
Daily compounding doubles the effective rate

subtopics.title: The Headline and the Till Slip

questions.question: In the shop picture, the nominal rate is the window sticker and the effective rate is:
options: The till slip — what your money actually grew by in a full year

questions.question: The till slip is computed by:
options: Adding the monthly rates for twelve months
Subtracting the compounding fee from the sticker
Sending one rand through the machine for a year — for example 1,0075 twelve times over
Dividing the sticker rate by the number of paydays

questions.question: Bank offers can only be compared fairly by:
options: Choosing the bank with more branches
Converting every offer to its effective rate and comparing those

questions.question: The laptop's rand price rising from R14 800 to R15 800 while staying $800 shows that:
options: A weakening rand raises the rand cost of imports even when foreign prices stand still
The shop added inflation to the sticker
